title: Generosity part 5
devotional:
2 Corinthians 8:1-9

‘’And now, brothers and sisters, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the Macedonian churches. In the midst of a very severe trial, their overflowing joy and their extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity. For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability. Entirely on their own, they urgently pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the Lord’s people. And they exceeded our expectations: They gave themselves first of all to the Lord, and then by the will of God also to us. So we urged Titus, just as he had earlier made a beginning, to bring also to completion this act of grace on your part. But since you excel in everything—in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness and in the love we have kindled in you—see that you also excel in this grace of giving. I am not commanding you, but I want to test the sincerity of your love by comparing it with the earnestness of others. For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.’’

As we have seen, the opportunity to be generous has nothing to do with the resources a person may or may not have. These Christians gave even though they were living in extreme poverty. The meaning behind these words is destitution. People often have a ‘if only’ attitude when it comes to generosity. They think ‘if only had I more I could do more, or give more.’ But this completely misses the point. If our hearts are full of grace and joy then even if we have little we will have enough to be generous. The important thing about this word used for poverty is that it is the same word that is used to describe the deliberate intention of the Lord Jesus. ‘For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that you through his poverty might become rich.’ 2 Corinthians 8:9

Their generosity was not caused by external pressure but internal desire. ‘For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability. Entirely on their own. They urgently pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.’ Often we see people begging for help, but these people were begging to give help.

Why would they be so eager to give?

The love of God was so much at work in the hearts of these people that it could not be contained. The extravagant, uncontainable generosity of God erupted out of their lives; it was a spontaneous expression of the ongoing work of God in their hearts. This is so freeing, because guilt and shame could never reproduce this kind of generosity. Guilt motivated generosity is like trying to feed the hungry with stale bread. Guilt defiles or soils generosity, it robs it of its glory or beauty, making it into a subtle expression of selfishness.

Their generosity to others, was consistent with giving themselves to the Lord. ‘They did not do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us in keeping with God’s will.’

Let me ask us this question, when did you last give yourself to the Lord?

I am not talking about conversion, but the continual ongoing giving of yourself to him.

Every one of us have opportunities and a need to live generous lives. We are never more alive or more God-like when we are displaying grace motivated generosity. There is only one thing that will prevent us from being generous and that is the condition of our hearts. Sometimes our lack of resources can be more of a help than a hindrance to generosity, for in having little to give we are more free to give ourselves. It is good to share financially with others, but sometimes in doing that we don’t really give ourselves.

Our English word for generous comes from the Latin generosus which means ‘of noble birth.’ Noble can mean an exalted moral character or excellence. I like that. Through our generosity, we give birth to a life that is distinguished, a life that is attractive, and a life that makes others stop and say ‘I wish I was like that!’
prayer: Father may I have a generous character
